data.description:
# Rebase-If-Necessary submits a tree CI never validated, so `main` can violate a LOCKED gate while every landed change was green

## What is broken on `main` right now

`src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` is **803 LOC on `gerrit/main`**, over the LOCKED 800-LOC
module-size cap. The gate scans every `src/rebar` file, so **any change whose patchset tree contains
that file fails `Verified`**:

```
##[error]src/rebar file(s) over the 800-LOC hard cap (split them — there is no allowlist):
803 src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py
```

It crossed the cap in `339262b990` ("af11: silence unrelated ambiguity in close scan"), merged
2026-08-04 16:28Z.

## The mechanism — how a green change landed a red tree

Change **1367** merged AFTER af11 and its merged commit carries the 803-line file. It nonetheless has
a legitimate `Verified +1`. Its module-size gate reported:

    Module-size gate: OK (no src/rebar file exceeds the 800-LOC hard cap; limit locked at 800).

Because the gate ran on the **patchset**, and the patchset was based on a commit predating af11:

```
tested patchset  refs/changes/67/1367/3
  base                929ba5d66940        transition_close.py = 800   -> gate OK
  af11 an ancestor?   NO
submitted commit    313b4e9fcf21
  parent              0d1c92a1027e        transition_close.py = 803   -> gate would FAIL
```

`main` is **Rebase-If-Necessary**, so Gerrit rebased at submit and landed a tree that **CI never
ran against**. The `Verified +1` was earned on a different tree than the one that merged.

**Three changes have landed this way since af11** — 1366, 1364, 1367 (16:53Z, 17:37Z, 17:39Z) — each
green on a pre-af11 base, each landing the 803-line file forward.

## Why this is a hole in the gate, not just an accident

The module-size limit is deliberately LOCKED: `.github/module-size-limit.txt` is single-sourced and a
normal contributor changing it fails CI, because "an administrator must override this gate to land a
limit change". The intent is that the cap cannot be crossed without an explicit administrative act.
Server-side rebase defeats that intent **without anyone overriding anything**: no administrator acted,
no gate was forced, and yet `main` now violates the locked invariant.

It also inverts the incentive. A change branched from CURRENT main is BLOCKED; a change sitting on a
stale base sails through and pushes the violation forward. The stalest branches are the ones that can
still land.

## Blast radius, and why it will get worse

Every change branched from af11 or later is blocked until the file is split. Epic
`e369-a449-4773-48fb` has **eight** such changes queued (1370, 1371, 1372, 1373, 1375, 1378, 1380,
1381), all `Verified -1` solely on this. As the pre-af11-based changes drain, the blocked set becomes
everything.

## Candidate remedies (a CI-policy decision, recorded not taken)

1. **Re-verify after rebase.** Make submit-time rebase re-trigger CI, or forbid Rebase-If-Necessary
   when the rebase changes any gated invariant. Correct but slows every submit.
2. **Evaluate the file-size gate against the MERGE RESULT** rather than the patchset tree, the way a
   conflict check already looks at both sides.
3. **Accept the window and detect it**: a post-merge job on `main` that fails loudly the moment a
   locked invariant is violated, so the breach is attributed to the merge that caused it instead of to
   the next contributor who happens to branch from it.

(3) is the cheapest and would have caught this at 16:28Z rather than leaving it to be diagnosed by an
agent whose unrelated changes it blocked.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `transition_close.py` is under the cap on `main` (immediate unblock; owned separately)
- [ ] a decision is recorded on whether submit-time rebase must re-verify, or whether the gate moves
      to the merge result
- [ ] `main` gains a check that fails when a LOCKED invariant is violated post-merge, attributing it
      to the merge commit
- [ ] a test pins that a patchset based on a stale base cannot land a tree violating the module-size
      cap — the specific hole demonstrated above

## Method note

I first told the operator "nothing can land until this is split". **That was too strong**, and the
evidence above is what corrected it: changes based on a pre-af11 main still pass and still land. The
accurate statement is that any change whose PATCHSET TREE contains the over-cap file is blocked. I
also briefly concluded the opposite — that those three had been force-submitted — from post-rebase
parents, which are not the tested tree; fetching `refs/changes/67/1367/3` directly is what settled it.
data.title: Rebase-If-Necessary submits a tree CI never validated, so main violates the LOCKED module-size cap while every landed change was green
